answer: Disjoint path persistence. An agent’s routing weight grows only when its traffic repeatedly crosses distinct, previously disjoint network neighborhoods. Each new identity must open a separate inlet route and sustain it across epochs before sending high-value messages. Relay assignments use an opal seed to prevent predictable placement. Attacker cost: every sybil needs its own long-lived paths and relay diversity; sharing a grove of relays collapses the weight, so each identity pays separate bandwidth, latency, and maintenance.
